full_context: A 50-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of severe lower chest pain for the past hour. The pain radiates to the back and is associated with nausea. He has had two episodes of non-bloody vomiting since the pain started. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. He drinks five to six beers per day. His medications include enalapril and metformin. His temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Examination shows a distended abdomen with epigastric tenderness and guarding but no rebound; bowel sounds are decreased.
